artworks.title: Picus and Circe
artworks.description: Giordano stages Circe's rejected courtship of Picus — the Latian king who stays faithful to Canens before the spell that turns him into a woodpecker.

artworks.title: Circe Turning King Picus into a Woodpecker
artworks.description: Lubieniecki paints Ovid's metamorphosis: Circe's wand raised as feathers break on Picus — the husband Canens will search the Laurentine shore for, singing until she wastes into air. National Museum in Warsaw.

artworks.title: Circe Changing Picus into a Bird
artworks.description: Metamorphoses plate: Circe's companions drive Picus as wings break from his body — the Ovidian crisis that strands Canens as the singing widow of Latium. Metropolitan Museum of Art.
